paragraphs: The Tranche 2 AML/CTF reforms bring real estate into scope from 1 July 2026. A legal determination is being sought on whether TPCH is itself a reporting entity. This scope readies the portal for the obligations that follow, under either outcome.

The portal is already the system of record for end-buyer personal information and the deal trail (reservations, EOIs, expected settlement, commission status). That makes it the natural place to evidence customer due diligence and record-keeping — whether the reporting entity turns out to be TPCH, our channel partners, or both.

sections.text: Build trigger: do not start Phase 2 until the legal threshold question is answered. Phase 1 items are low-regret and can proceed once approved.
What changes depending on the legal answer

rows: TPCH is a reporting entity
Portal must capture and evidence CDD, source-of-funds and beneficial ownership, support record-keeping and reporting, and gate the EOI/contract-order step on CDD completion.
Only partners are reporting entities
Portal should help partners discharge their CDD and record-keeping (status fields, evidence storage, export) and must not impede it. TPCH-level gating is optional.
Neither (TPCH advised outside scope)
Phase 1 record-keeping and privacy items still recommended as good practice; Phase 2 controls deferred.

sections.text: Build regardless of the legal answer

rows: 1. 7-year retention
Confirm no flow hard-deletes buyer records. The 48-hour expiry should only flip status, not delete the row. Document a 7-year retention policy for reservations, EOIs and deals.
reservations, partner_deals tables; retention note in docs/
2. Consent timestamp
Make buyer-consent an explicit recorded checkbox with a timestamp at reservation, not just an agreement clause. Store who confirmed it.
reservation modal in index.html; reservations table
3. Audit trail
Log every create/change to buyer PII and CDD status — actor, field, before/after, timestamp. Extend the existing activity log rather than build new.
partner_activity_log
4. Record export
Admin-only export of reservations / deals with their CDD evidence to CSV, for an auditor or AUSTRAC request.
new admin export; service-role edge function

sections.text: Build if TPCH (or partners, via the portal) is captured

rows: 5. CDD status on the deal
Add fields: cdd_status (not started / in progress / verified), cdd_completed_by, cdd_completed_at, id_doc_type, verification_method. Surface a CDD badge on the deal and reservation cards.
reservations / partner_deals tables; deal + reservation UI
6. EOI / contract-order gate
Optionally block conversion to EOI (and the contract order) until CDD is marked verified. Make the gate a configurable setting so it can be switched on if TPCH is the reporting entity.
EOI conversion flow
7. Source of funds / wealth
Structured fields to record source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence against the buyer on the reservation/EOI.
new columns on reservations or a related table
8. Beneficial ownership
Capture underlying ownership/control where the buyer is a company, trust or SMSF (the portal already flags smsf_eligible stock).
reservation/EOI data model
9. Partner enrolment tracking
Fields on the partner record: austrac_enrolled (bool), austrac_re_number, enrolment_date, aml_program_in_place. Show an admin warning badge for partners transacting without enrolment.
channel_partners table; admin partner view
10. Suspicious-matter flag
Let staff or a partner flag a transaction for internal review and route it to TPCH admin. This is an internal trigger only — it does NOT lodge an SMR; that is done in AUSTRAC Online.
new flag on reservation/deal; admin queue

items: New columns on existing tables (reservations, partner_deals, channel_partners) are grandfathered for Data API access. Any brand-new table must include explicit GRANTs — from 30 Oct 2026 a new public table is invisible to PostgREST without them (see CLAUDE.md).

Buyer PII and CDD evidence are sensitive. Keep RLS tight: partners see only their own clients’ records; CDD evidence files (if stored) should sit in a private Storage bucket with signed-URL access, not a public bucket.
All migrations land in db/migrations/ and are pasted into the Supabase SQL editor (no CLI runner).
Several Phase 2 items (5, 9) are partner-noticeable and would warrant a CHANGELOG entry when shipped; Phase 1 items are largely internal.
The AML/CTF program document itself — that is drafted with the lawyer / AML consultant, not built in the portal.
Actual SMR / threshold-transaction lodgement — done in AUSTRAC Online, not the portal.
Selecting and integrating a KYC/identity-verification vendor — a separate decision once the obligation owner is confirmed.
Any handling of buyer funds or payments — TPCH does not, and this scope does not introduce it.
Now: get the legal determination (separate brief). Approve Phase 1.
On legal answer: confirm the obligation owner, then scope Phase 2 items that apply and choose a KYC vendor if needed.
Before 1 July 2026: if TPCH is captured, enrol with AUSTRAC, stand up the AML/CTF program, and switch on the EOI/CDD gate.

sections.text: This is a build scope, not legal advice. The obligation set is provisional until the legal determination lands; treat field lists as a starting point to refine with the adviser.
